criteria.requirement: No production code distinguishes a ledger approval from any other object by a scope string, a constructor, a prototype, an instanceof test or any value readable off the object: there is no class brand and no reachable constructor anywhere in the discriminator path. Every approval is built with Object.create(null), carries no scope field, holds primitives only (no Date, Buffer, typed array, Map, Set or function — timestamps are epoch-millisecond integers), and is deep-frozen with every nested object also null-prototype and frozen; a failure of the frozen, null-prototype or field-type assertion is PILOT_INTERNAL_ERROR exit 18, approval_not_sealed. ApprovalStore exposes no writer; the interactive ledger writer is an entry-only module which, when loaded by Node's ordinary require in a process whose entry is something else and whose require.main has not been reassigned to a Module object for the writer's own resolved path, exports no callable member of any name (exit 1, approve_writer_not_entry); entry identity is not claimed to be unforgeable against in-process code, because re-evaluating the source through vm, or constructing a Module for the writer path and assigning it to process.mainModule before calling its load, makes the module body run, so the writer's refusals must each be self-sufficient (exit 1, approve_writer_not_entry), reached only by falcon.js --approve-action after falcon.js asserts it is itself the process entry (else exit 1, falcon_not_entry), and which refuses unless CI and GITHUB_ACTIONS are unset, tty.isatty(0) and tty.isatty(1) hold by syscall, a prompt bound to the plan digest, role, origin, method, canonical path, manifest digest, build id and approvals root real path is rendered before the challenge is generated, and that freshly generated random challenge is typed back on fd 0 with no parameter, option, environment key, config key or file by which it can be supplied; every prompt rendered, including each refusal, is appended to the audit chain. The writer itself, and not falcon.js on its behalf, runs the key-carrier-flag rejection and a literal closed argv allowlist before any prompt and before any filesystem access, refusing any other token including a bare positional, a repeated flag and an abbreviated flag, with exit 1 and the reason named.
